text_fidelity_a:
Sennheiser PXC 450 Active Noise-Canceling Headphones I spend a great deal of time in a computer lab where there is literally over 1,000 running systems. In this environment, ear protection isn't absolutely necessary but without it there's some discomfort with which to deal because of all the fans in these systems and the requisite air handling units. I already have a pair of Bose QC-15 headphones but I am not a huge fan, so I recently purchased a pair of Sennheiser PXC-450 headphones for use in this environment. After an initial break-in period, I have come to really appreciate them.

This is going to be a comparative review, though primarily about the Sennheiser phones. Bose is generally regarded as the gold standard when it comes to ANC headphones, so matching the Sennheisers to the Bose is a good match-up. I'll break it all down into categories: Noise Canceling, Comfort, Sound Quality and Build Quality.

Noise Canceling:
Active noise canceling is THE primary feature of these phones and each has its strengths. Bose is, without question, the more capable ANC set when it comes to removing noise. This supremacy comes at a price though - because of the aggressiveness of their ANC, the wearer often feels a "pressure" on the ears when using the phones, something not present with the Sennheiser set which is close to Bose's level of canceling. Where Bose went to extremes to eliminate noise, Sennheiser went with the thought of "good enough for most". To be sure, both sets do a nice job of eliminating low frequency noise, enough to make air travel more pleasant if you dislike the rumble of plane engines.

They work in the car too (if you're not driving). I tried both sets in a moving vehicle and all do a fine job of eliminating road and engine noise. In fact, it was quiet to the point of eerie in the car. So, if you're a passenger on a long trip, either of these will work to suit your needs.

For the Sennheisers, you don't have to use ANC to listen to music as they provide the ability to override ANC and work like normal headphones. Bose, on the other hand, is an all-or-nothing deal and requires ANC to be on when listening to anything at all.

And that brings up a nice little feature on the Sennheisers - the "talk-thru" function, which allows a listener to cut off all sound and turn on a small microphone so that one can carry on a conversation without having to remove the headphones. No other headset I have ever used has this feature and it has already proven to be a handy tool.

Both sets require a single AAA battery to provide ANC. The battery life is definitely better with the Bose - mine last about a week between needing new batteries, whereas the Sennheiser set needs a new battery every other day.

Comfort:
The Sennheisers are the most comfortable headphones I have ever worn - period. The padding is buttery soft and they fit over my ears with no issue. Other reviewers have said that it seems like they just melt into your head, and that's a very accurate way to describe them. The Bose are nearly as comfortable, though they are slightly smaller.

Where the Sennheisers have a slight comfort disadvantage is actually in their size. These are big headphones and when they are worn around the neck instead of on the ears, they tend to rub on the neck and sometimes (depending on what you're doing) they can get in the way. If you take them off, or don't wear them around your neck, there's nothing about which to complain.

Sound Quality:
Sennheiser has always had premium sound, and the PXC-450 headphones demonstrate why they are the champs when it comes to quality sound. Though not audiophile phones, the PXC-450 brings awesome sound quality even at low volumes, with very full midrange and decent bass. The Bose sound great, except that the bass is too rich and without an equalizer in the mix the bass is enough to give me a headache over extended periods.

Build Quality:
I have not had the Sennheiser set very long but so far I have had no trouble with them. They feel rugged and sturdy, though they are mostly plastic so they do scratch and twist easily. The cord is heavy gauge wire, a welcome improvement over the cabling on Sennheiser sets I have worn in the past. The Bose set is a little more flimsy, with lesser gauge wire.

In summary, I find that the Sennheiser PXC-450 headphones are a better product than the Bose QC-15 headphones. They sound great, feel comfortable and they do a fine job of canceling noise. Bose does have better ANC and if that is the main thing you need and you don't mind the sensation of pressure they put on the ears then Bose is a better choice, but in almost every other aspect the Sennheisers bring more to the table.
text_fidelity_b: Sennheiser PXC 450 Active Noise-Canceling Headphones

This is just what I needed to store extra cords I don't use as often but still have them handy.

When I got the laptop it came with a dongle that allowed me to connect the the ethernet cable through my USB port. It worked great but took away one of the USB ports and also made it difficult to plug anything else into the port next to it.
I had been looking for something different and when I did a search I must have looked at 10-15 of them. This one caught my eye because it had three USB 3.0 ports, and it got a lot of great reviews so I gave it a try. I've had it now for about a month and it works great.
It allows me to connect to my network with an ethernet cable which gives me a lot better speeds than WiFi, and it gives me three USB 3.0 ports that I can use for anything I need to plug into the computer. The ports are spread out on the device so that I can actually plug three things in, which is an added bonus. The problem I had in the past was that I needed to use a device to read several types of SD cards, and the device is so large it can't really be plugged into my laptop USB ports. With the uni dongle I have no problems and it works great.
So, if you are looking for an ethernet to USB dongle, this one is highly recommended.

text_fidelity_a:
Epson E11E223052 ProSense 367 GPS Multisport Watch with Ultra Long Battery Life and Sapphire Glass - Black I run during the summer and run outside. I hate carrying heavy items with me, like water bottles and phones. I feel they sort of hinder my performance, though I realize it's probably more psychological than physical.
Still, I'm not going to mess with a run I've been accustomed to for nearly twenty years, but I do wish, more often than not, that I had some way of tracking my run and how many miles I've done *exactly* while being outside. Sure, I can track the mileage by checking my phone before and after, but it would be nice to have a tracker on me without adding any psychological weight. I used to have a Polar watch that worked fine, but it died some time ago and I never bothered to get a replacement.
But finally I did.

With this one, I'm able to wear the watch without toting my phone along and it still carries all the features and tracking as if the phone were connected to any other tracking watch. While this watch is used for a number of cardio activities, I use it only for running. There are "pages" of exercises you can track, but for a quick run the default is set on the bottom left button--very nice to have, especially for me. Not sure if you can change the default on there to another exercise, but for me it's perfect and I haven't bothered looking up how to change it.
But curious to check out the full features, I ventured into the different pages (or screens) the watch has to offer. During my course, I found that the buttons were *very* stiff. This might be to prevent accidental presses during exercise, but I found that I had to press almost twice has hard as other electronic watches for the watch to recognize my press. But, from my uses so far, I've pressed it mostly to view all the screens when testing out all the features. When actually running, I do no more than a few presses before and after each run. The network had trouble activating itself in the beginning, but that's because I was fiddling with it outside. It kept trying to set itself numerous times when I actually ran outside, but I always dismissed it. Once, however, I was under the open sky I let it connect and it has had no problem or delay connecting ever since.

After every run I am able to sync it with the Epson app, as well as RunKeeper. People have complained about the Epson app but I find it neat and useful.

Overall, it's a great little watch that accurately records my runs and uploads them without the use of the phone during the workout. I'm able to review it speedily on my phone right after, and I love that I can now track my progress without the burden of added weight. It's pricey for sure, but considering I don't need my phone and my previous watch lasted me ten years, I'm sure this watch will be a great investment that will last me hopefully for another decade or so.
text_fidelity_b: Epson E11E223052 ProSense 367 GPS Multisport Watch with Ultra Long Battery Life and Sapphire Glass - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Sony MDREX38iP/BLK EX Earbud with iPod Remote Control - Black For moderate priced earbuds, these are pretty good. The sound quality is much better than average, with smooth response across the range. The highs are detailed, and not shrill. The midbass is clear, with no unnatural peak that sometimes passes for "bass boost". The deep bass is natural, and not artificially strong. Very easy to listen to for extended sessions.

For comfort, these are pretty average -- not the best comfort, but not bad either. There are interchangeable ear tips you can try out for the best fit. There's a lot of personal preference as to what's going to stay in the ear comfortably. The earbuds are angled, so you have to pay attention to the left/right orientation.

This is advertised as "iPhone compatible", meaning that there's a mic with tiny + and - buttons attached to the left ear piece. I'm a BlackBerry guy, and I'm happy to report that the mic works fine with my BlackBerry Bold 9700. But the + and - buttons don't have any effect (they don't raise or lower the volume). However, pressing the small button between the + and - buttons will either pause the song that's playing, or mute a phone call. Pretty handy.

Sound isolation is not a strong point of this set. I wasn't sure what to expect, so I guess I'm not disappointed. Probably you'd want to look elsewhere if sound isolation is important to you.

Durability may also be an issue. The wire is very thin, and it feels fragile, especially where it connects to the earbud. I'll know in 6 to 12 months whether these will stand up to regular use. The 90-degree plug will take wear better for many people, depending on how it connects to your phone, MP3 player or computer. Comes with a little storage pouch, which is good protection for the set when not in use.
text_fidelity_b: Sony MDREX38iP/BLK EX Earbud with iPod Remote Control - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Nulaxy Bluetooth Car FM Transmitter Audio Adapter Receiver Wireless Handsfree Voltmeter Car Kit TF Card AUX 1.44 Display – KM18 Peacock Blue *UPDATED REVIEW*

A seller replaced a different defective FM transmitter unit with this one for me (mine has the Kollea brand name on it, but this is the identical unit, private-labeled). This is a better product than what it replaced, but is not without it's flaws. I have three (*UPDATE: now four, and the fourth one is a deal-breaker--see below) complaints with this unit:

1) It will not automatically reconnect to my phone about 75% of the time. I have to manually shut Bluetooth off and turn it back on on the phone, sometimes a few times before it pairs successfully. This is a hassle--a PITA. Every time I get in the car, I have to go through this process--every time power is cut from the transmitter, actually, so if your passenger knocks it and it pops out of the 12V socket, it will have to be re-paired, which is supposed to happen automatically, but does not, and you then have to go through the process. Frustrating.

2) Charge output is only 1.0A. this is why I returned the first one--phone gives a "slow charging" warning when charging from this unit, regardless of what USB cable I use (I tried four different cables, all of which I know for certain can carry 2.1A).

3) Callers have occasionally complained they cannot hear me well when using this unit, and I occasionally (but not often) encounter FM interference. I believe Bluetooth itself is part of the problem, and anyone who has used a few Bluetooth headsets or units like this knows audio quality is terrible. Period. We just deal with it. Add to that the burden of having to transmit your signal via FM to a car stereo and the user-side audio (what you will hear in your car) is always going to be craptastic.

4) (*UPDATE) When paired, voice recognition on my phone, which is usually quite good, becomes severely impaired. This is also likely the culprit for complaint #3, above. I suspect this is because when paired, it tries to use the built-in microphone for voice recognition instead of the microphones on my phone (of which there are 4). It is disabling the extremely good microphones in my phone (Nokia lumia Icon which is well known for having incredible audio input) and using the unit's crappy microphone instead. This microphone is located in the unit, which is attached to the center console of my car near the shifter, and thus picks up all the vibrations and related road and engine noise transmitted through the structure of the car as I drive. This approach is terrible. I have stopped using the unit for anything requiring voice input, including telephone calls. In other words, this is just a big awkward charger now, and one that charges painfully slowly (see complaint #2). If it were possible to disable the onboard mic, and use the mics in my phone instead for calls and voice recognition, this would be a much more serviceable unit As it is now, it is just a piece of junk.

Cannot recommend this item. There are definitely worse products out there. I have not tried them all, but of those I have used, this is the best one so far. I will likely keep using it until the lack of automatic pairing pushes me over the edge with it one day and I get something else. (*UPDATE: this thing just does not work well, and I am now looking for something else.)
text_fidelity_b: Nulaxy Bluetooth Car FM Transmitter Audio Adapter Receiver Wireless Handsfree Voltmeter Car Kit TF Card AUX 1.44 Display – KM18 Peacock Blue

This is a decent TV mount for large TVs but could be better.

text_fidelity_a:
Screwdriver Set for MacBook, Tri-Wing Phillips Pentalobe 5 Pentalobe T5 Pentalobe T6 Screwdrivers Repair Tool Kit for Apple MacBook Mac Retina Pro Air This tool set is almost perfect! I’ll start with a little background... I am tech savvy for the most part, and I refurbish my own electronics, as well as stuff for friends and family from time to time. My MacBook Pro was bogged down by a “feature” known as thermal throttling. When older thermal paste dries up, it fails to conduct heat as well, so performance takes a nose dive in favor of preservation.

I’m not entirely sure if Apple actually does this servicing upon request, or not, but I honestly wouldn’t think that they do. So, after figuring out what was going on with my laptop, I rolled up my sleeves, brought out the few electronics tools I had around, and proceeded to gut my MacBook. Bad idea. You ever hear that saying about not bringing a knife to a gunfight? It went about that well.

Long story short, I busted a clip off of the motherboard that would have held the keyboard ribbon cable in place, and you can’t really just replace the clip on a motherboard, you have to replace the entire board. If I had this tool set in time for that repair, I could have saved the cost of replacing the board.

That said, these arrived in time for me to do the motherboard swap, and before I did (managed to upgrade to the i7 processor from the i5, a mild boost in performance I’m sure.) I made sure to once again, remove the heat sync, and remove the old thermal paste, replacing it with fresh TG-7. My geekbench scores now come in above what is average for the i7 version of my MacBook Pro. Above average is virtually unheard of. It’s like a brand new machine.

But these tools, if you attempt to do a repair without them, you could end up costing yourself a few hundred extra dollars. Learn from my mistake!

My only negatives here are for the durability and sturdiness, because I feel like the plastic spudger thing is definitely going to break eventually at the sharp pointy side. I don’t trust the plastic much. Other than that, the kit is well worth it, and every Mac enthusiast who plans to repair their own machine should really have it.
text_fidelity_b: Screwdriver Set for MacBook, Tri-Wing Phillips Pentalobe 5 Pentalobe T5 Pentalobe T6 Screwdrivers Repair Tool Kit for Apple MacBook Mac Retina Pro Air

I've tried to upgrade earbuds (nothing too pricey) and have always been disappointed.

🏋🏼‍♀️ I wear them while I work out. They have a great sound and block outside noise pretty well. They help me get in my zone in my own little world, and I love them.

💦 I tried to swim in them, and while they're waterproof, they stop playing as soon as my head is underwater.

🎧 The plastic ear tips, which are super comfortable for my tiny ear holes, eventually broke down — as aging plastic will do. I replaced them with BLLQ Replacement Ear Tips, which are nearly identical to the originals [[ASIN:B07FF9DN5K BLLQ Replacement Ear Tips]].

💵 They're $20. BT 4.1. So not the newest Bluetooth, and I'm sure Bose sounds better. But at this price point, I love these little guys.

🏆 Actually, I got them on a lightning sale for $13, so even better! So I paid $20 for the earbuds AND replacement tips.

🌚 I still want something new because I just want something new, you know. But knowing the disappointment I always feel with my attempted replacements, I'll probably keep using these sweet little babies.

🔊 I don't know what the heck they're talking about with the "noise canceling" in the product title. There is no ACTIVE noise-canceling, but the earbuds do form slight seals, which have a passive noise-canceling effect. I think I actually bought them for noise-canceling, but whatever. It's overrated as a feature unless you are willing to pay hundreds of dollars.

In sum, these are great earbuds, especially if you're prone to losing things and hate to feel heartbroken about losing something expensive.

TP-Link AC1900 Touch Screen Wi-Fi Gigabit Router We replaced an older router with this one to take advantage of better speeds and slightly better coverage. This router has 3 antennas and the signal seems to be a little stronger in the furthest rooms than with our old router.

Physically the router is about 30% bigger than the average home routers we’ve owned, but it does have 3 antennas and a touch screen that's about the size of a smaller iPhone screen. It also has holes in the back for wall mounting.

We don’t use a lot of the advanced features that this router offers, such as mode-switching to a repeater, or the parental controls (it's not like the cats are going to surf the net... at least as far as we know), but it's there if you want it. The touch-screen did make it super-easy to setup. There's no need to connect a laptop to it, everything can be setup right on the screen which is nice.

Overall our usage of a router is pretty basic. Just set in and forget it, and so far it's been reliable considering the amount of gaming and streaming we do.

Getting used to the pen (it is NOT a mouse) and figuring out what shortcuts are worth programming was a whole 'nuther trip. Disabling the Windows Pen and Touch long hold feature that turns into a right click was another adventure. THEN figuring out how to manipulate the brushes to get the effects for drawing... oye.

I'm an artist, and I use Photoshop, illustrator, indesign, and sketchbook pro. Moving from a basic stylus, and mouse to the pen has been a revelation. You CAN teach an old dog new tricks! Sony HT-S350 Soundbar with Wireless Subwoofer: S350 2.1ch Sound Bar and Powerful Subwoofer - Home Theater Surround Sound Speaker System for TV - Blutooth and HDMI Arc Compatible Bar Black I paired this sound bar with our Sony XBR-65X850E 65” TV and it could not have been easier.

While my TV would allow me to connect to the sound bar via Bluetooth I opted to connect via the HDMI ARC connection to avoid any sound lag. In addition to these 2 connection options you can connect via the included optical cable.

I followed the instructions - plugged the HDMI cable (not included) into the ARC HDMI port, plugged the sound bar and subwoofer into the surge protector and turned everything on. The TV automatically recognized the soundbar and changed my output.

All I had to do was press the “secure link” button on the remote and the sound bar wirelessly linked to the subwoofer without issue.

I decided to move the subwoofer to another area of the room - I unplugged it, moved it, plugged it back in and it reconnected without any problem.

I was able to pair the system with my iPhone without any issue and the sound is stunning. From the rich bass of the subwoofer, the vibrant midtones, to the crisp highs - every note is clear and distinct.

While I have a true 5.1 surround system most of the TV broadcasts are not going to utilize that type of system and the sound is actually richer through a sound bar with a subwoofer.

This soundbar can be easily wall mounted using the included template.

The entire system is intuitive and user friendly. While many sound systems require hours to hook up and figure out how to use correctly this one is so straightforward. The remote doesn’t have a bunch of excess buttons that you’ll never need or use.

In my instance my TV remote was able to control it immediately with no issues.

I highly recommend this soundbar for anyone looking for an easy way to improve the quality of the sound from your TV - and you’ll be pleasantly surprised by the rich sound it will deliver regardless of what you play through it.

My tablets go everywhere with me and I use them in a variety of places.....the car, the horse barn, outside on the patio, and they travel in my hand bag, luggage and saddle bags. I need real protection and a flat back on the cases. For me, this skeleton thing just doesn't work as well as a regular folio case.
